To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
• • • • • Implicit learning is a process that occurs in the background of our minds.
“Journalists’ tacit knowledge is the result of implicit learning and is a source of intuition”.

1) The most important competencies for future newsroom journalists, as identified by mid-career journalists, are the ability to write well and the ability to work with others; 2) The most important skills for future newsroom journalism, as identified by our mid-career journalists are writing skills, computer skills and people skills; and 3) The most important knowledge for future newsroom news journalists is the ability to use the internet and knowledge of the law.
In summary, our research is concerned with
tacit knowledge and intuition as they relate to journalism and journalism education.
tacit knowledge and the role it plays in the acquisition of professional skills and competencies in journalism.
the acquisition of knowledge by journalists, and the nature of that knowledge.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
implicit knowledge is the knowledge that is gained from the experience of the environment.
tacit knowledge is a type of knowledge that is acquired without conscious, reflective strategies.
implicit learning, and the tacit knowledge that is its result, is a form of knowledge that is not accessible to consciousness, and that is not available for explication.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
implicit learning is the acquisition of knowledge without conscious awareness of the process of acquisition, and without conscious awareness of knowledge acquired (Reber, in Smith and Kosslyn, 2008).
implicit learning and tacit knowledge are the basis of intuition.
tacit knowledge is acquired through experience, and is not available to conscious thought or reflection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the news industry has a problem.
implicit knowledge can be used to make sense of how journalists work.
journalists need to develop the skills and competencies to identify and understand the implicit processes and knowledge that they use.
